To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the tumor-associated immune cell infiltrate at the periphery of the primary MCC is a robust prognosticator for survival and that this infiltrate is more prominent in MCPyV-positive MCCs.

1) higher CD3 and CD8 T-cell density at tumor periphery is associated with improved survival; 2) higher CD8 T-cell infiltrate is a robust prognosticator in MCC; 3) MCPyV+ MCCs have more robust immune infiltrates; and 4) MCPyV status and immune infiltrate are associated with improved survival in MCPyV+ cases.
